after: Their insight can faintly sound as an inward excellence beside the separate act of making deeds attractive.
reason: مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ names inner perception, which gives a weak route to B001's faultless inner excellence. The verse says they had insight, not that this insight was beautiful, so the link stays a note.

after: The beautified deeds carry an ethical echo of excellence, reaching beyond visual charm.
reason: وَزَيَّنَ supplies the beauty field, while 29:46's أَحْسَنُ explicitly names what is best or most excellent. That ethical excellence can also be heard through B001's dictionary sense of beauty as a quality without blemish, making the latent evaluation available.

after: The Fatiha's opening name-form faintly evokes beauty as a visible identifying mark.
reason: بِسْمِ means 'in the name,' a naming formula that faintly evokes the B001 gloss of beauty whose trace appears on a person through the listed وَسْم route. The Fatiha does not name visible beauty here, so the connection remains weak.

after: The adornment becomes a false-facing surface that turns its bearers away from the recognized road.
reason: وَزَيَّنَ makes the deeds attractive, and the following فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ gives that attraction a consequence: it diverts them. B002's image of beauty made visible can therefore be heard as a worked-over, misleading surface rather than a real improvement.

after: Beautification can be faintly heard as making something visible beside the clear appearance of the ruins.
reason: تَّبَيَّنَ says the evidence from the dwellings became clear, which calls the visibility facet of B002's making beauty appear. Clarity is not beauty, so the trigger supports only a note.

after: Their stated insight makes the polished appearance of their deeds audible as something seen yet misleading.
reason: The focus has وَزَيَّنَ, the act of making something look beautiful, and مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ names their perceptive sight. Together they let the branch's visual appearance resonate ironically: the people had insight, yet the deeds were made attractive enough to divert them.

after: Their deeds can be faintly heard as crafted presentation, though the later verb only names making or doing.
reason: تَصْنَعُونَ names what people make or do; beside وَزَيَّنَ it gives a weak crafted-appearance route into B002's active beautification. The later word itself does not say that the thing made is beautiful.

after: A possible morning reading lends a faint light-and-display image to beautification.
reason: فَأَصْبَحُوا۟ can carry a morning sense as well as 'they became,' and B002 includes natural light as a way beauty is shown. In this clause 'they became' is straightforward, so the light image is only a weak trigger.

after: The word for truth faintly calls the branch's act of making a quality manifest.
reason: بِٱلْحَقِّ names truth in God's creation, and B002 also includes bringing a quality into view. This gives a weak manifestation link, but the verse does not say that truth itself is beautified.

after: The attractive deeds take on an ethical echo of doing something well or making it better.
reason: أَحْسَنُ in 29:46 evaluates the manner of argument as best, directly calling improvement and doing well. B002 includes improving a thing, performing work well, and beneficence, so the explicit evaluation activates that enhancement sense beside وَزَيَّنَ.

after: The command to look gives a weak visual route to beauty being presented to an observer.
reason: فَٱنظُرُوا۟ directs the audience to look at the earth and the beginning of creation, which weakly calls B002's image of an appearance made visible. The verse asks them to inspect origins rather than describing adornment.

after: The deceptive improvement of deeds sits against the Fatiha's explicit bestowal of good favor.
reason: B002 includes doing good for another, and أَنْعَمْتَ in the Fatiha explicitly names the bestowal of favor. That word activates the branch's beneficent-improvement facet, giving وَزَيَّنَ a moral contrast with the actual good bestowed on the guided.

after: The Fatiha's nurturing Lord faintly evokes natural growth that brings beauty into view.
reason: رَبِّ names the Lord who nurtures and brings things to completion, a weak conceptual path to B002's image of the earth flourishing with growth. The Fatiha does not mention plants or beautification, so this remains only a note.

after: Their collected deeds can be faintly heard as inward qualities displayed like adornment.
reason: أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ names their collected deeds, which can represent inward qualities a person displays; B003 expressly includes inward qualities among adornments. Deeds are not literally ornaments here, so this extension from action to inner decoration is only a note.

before: The ruins of their dwellings are evidence (plain).
after: Their former homes can faintly sound as worldly possessions that once gave a people stature.
reason: مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ names tangible dwellings, and B003 extends adornment to external worldly goods and furnishings. These ruined homes are evidence rather than decorative objects, so the material-possession image is weak.

after: What people make faintly evokes cultivated appearance, although no ornament is named.
reason: The listed صُنْع pairing evokes a crafted bearing and adornment, while B003 names qualities and objects used for ornament. تَصْنَعُونَ itself only says 'you make or do,' so it weakly hints at cultivated appearance without naming an ornament.

after: The self-sufficient one faintly evokes the dictionary's figure who has no need of adornment.
reason: لَغَنِىٌّ gives self-sufficiency, while the listed غَنِيَة branch describes a woman dispensed with the need for adornment. The surah word describes God's absolute independence rather than a woman's ornament, so the ornament-free image is weak.

after: The Fatiha's obedient belief system can weakly resonate as an inward adornment.
reason: ٱلدِّينِ in the Fatiha names obedience and a belief system; B003 includes inner belief among the qualities that may adorn a person. The verse does not call religion an ornament, so this is a weak inward-quality bridge.
